title: Derived ringed-topos direct image preserves compatible central scalars
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Suppose given unital homomorphisms $s_A:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$ and $s_B:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,B)$ whose restrictions $s_A(r)|_U\in A(U)$ and $s_B(r)|_V\in B(V)$ are central for every $r\in R$ and every site object $U\in\mathcal C$, $V\in\mathcal D$, and such that the structural map $c:u^{-1}A\to B$ carries $u^{-1}s_A(r)$ to $s_B(r)$ for every $r\in R$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] define $(r f)_U(x)=s_A(r)|_U f_U(x)$, and likewise using $s_B$. Equip the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the induced $R$-linear structures [def-weil-linear-category, lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. The canonical K-injective derived direct image $Ru_*:D(B)\to D(A)$, computed with the derived-functor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. In particular it sends the endomorphism induced by the actual scalar section $s_B(r)$ to that induced by $s_A(r)$; no exactness of $u_*$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies), computation of the right derived functor on K-injectives. The compatible-central-scalar assertion is the implicit compatible-central-scalar prerequisite.

proof.text: First check the stated scalar structures on module sheaves. For $A$-modules $M,N$ and $f:M\to N$, centrality gives $(r f)_U(a x)=s_A(r)|_U a f_U(x)=a s_A(r)|_U f_U(x)$; hence $r f$ is $A$-linear. It commutes with restrictions because both the scalar section and $f$ do. The additive and scalar axioms on each Hom group follow sectionwise from the module axioms and the unital ring map $s_A$. For composable module maps, $g\circ(r f)=r(g\circ f)=(r g)\circ f$, since $g$ is $A$-linear. Thus these Hom groups give the stated $R$-linear category; the same calculation with $B$ gives its $R$-linear category. Local centrality, rather than commutativity of $R$ alone, is what makes $r f$ a module morphism.

source.place: Tags 09MJ (definition-linear-category), 09MK (definition-functor-linear-categories); elementary sectionwise verification of the prescribed central action

proof.text: Put $F=u_*:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$. Its underlying additive sheaf functor and $A$-action are those in the ringed-topos morphism definition. A generalized element $x$ of $FN$ has an adjoint transpose $\widetilde x$ in $N$. By that action formula and the compatibility hypothesis, the transpose of $s_A(r)x$ is $c(u^{-1}s_A(r))\widetilde x=s_B(r)\widetilde x$. Naturality of the sheaf adjunction in $N$ therefore identifies the transposes of $F(r f)(x)$ and $s_A(r)F(f)(x)$ for every module morphism $f$. They are equal, so $F(r f)=rF(f)$. The given additive direct image also has $F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g)$. This proves $R$-linearity of the underived module functor without assuming that the geometric morphism comes from a functor between the sites.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward); the adjoint-transpose action formula in def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism

proof.text: The smallness hypothesis makes $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ Grothendieck abelian by the arbitrary-ring-sheaf theorem. The K-injective existence theorem therefore supplies a quasi-isomorphism $a:N\to I$ for every complex $N$, with $I$ K-injective. Apply $F$ degreewise. Its additivity sends a homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$ to the same equation for $Ff,Fg,Fh$ and identifies the cone differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d&f\\0&-d\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with the corresponding differential after $F$; finite biproducts are preserved by an additive functor. Thus $Q_A F:K(B)\to D(A)$ respects shifts and cone triangles, hence is exact as a functor of triangulated categories. The total-derived theorem applies to this functor and gives the canonical $RF=Ru_*$ and comparison $\eta_I:Q_A(FI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(Q_B I)$ for K-injective $I$. Exactness here concerns cone triangles, not exactness of $F$ on module sheaves.

Fix complexes $N,N\prime$ and resolutions $a:N\to I$, $b:N\prime\to J$. Write $c_a=\eta_I^{-1}\circ RF(Q_Ba)$ and $c_b=\eta_J^{-1}\circ RF(Q_Bb)$. For every derived morphism $h:Q_BN\to Q_BN\prime$, the arbitrary-resolution computation theorem gives a unique homotopy class $g:I\to J$ satisfying $Q_Bg=(Q_Bb)\circ h\circ(Q_Ba)^{-1}$ and $c_b\circ RF(h)\circ c_a^{-1}=Q_A(Fg)$. Here $Fg$ can be computed with any chain-map representative. These are the specified derived-functor comparisons, so they compute the canonical $Ru_*$ rather than a newly chosen functor. By the linear-derived-category theorem, $Q_A,Q_B$ preserve addition and the componentwise central scalar action.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); arbitrary-resolution formula as stated in lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation

proof.text: Use the same resolutions for two parallel derived morphisms $h,k$, represented by homotopy classes $g,t:I\to J$ as in the preceding step. Choose chain-map representatives for $g,t$. Linearity of $Q_B$ and bilinearity of composition show that $r g$ represents $r h$ and $g+t$ represents $h+k$: for example $Q_B(r g)=r\big((Q_Bb)h(Q_Ba)^{-1}\big)=(Q_Bb)(r h)(Q_Ba)^{-1}$. By the comparison formula and the degreewise calculation of step 2, $$c_b RF(r h)c_a^{-1}=Q_A(F(r g))=Q_A(r Fg)=r\big(c_b RF(h)c_a^{-1}\big).$$ Cancel the fixed comparison isomorphisms using $R$-bilinearity of composition to obtain $RF(rh)=rRF(h)$. The identical calculation with $g+t$ gives $c_b RF(h+k)c_a^{-1}=Q_A(Fg)+Q_A(Ft)=c_b(RF(h)+RF(k))c_a^{-1}$, hence $RF(h+k)=RF(h)+RF(k)$. All derived objects admit complex representatives by the definition of $D(B)$ (or its essentially surjective localization); conjugation by any presentation isomorphisms preserves these two equalities by bilinearity. Thus the conclusion holds for every pair of derived objects.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y, via the cited arbitrary-resolution formula; elementary linear calculation with that formula

proof.text: The two equalities just proved say that $Ru_*$ is an $R$-linear functor. On a complex $N$, multiplication by the actual global section $s_B(r)$ is the chain endomorphism $r\operatorname{id}_N$, whose derived image is $r\operatorname{id}_{Q_BN}$ because $Q_B$ is linear. Consequently $Ru_*(r\operatorname{id})=r\operatorname{id}_{Ru_*N}$; on the representative $F I$ this is multiplication by the actual section $s_A(r)$, by step 2. This proves also the final scalar-endomorphism assertion.

Verdict PASS, with no changes. Shape: one commit; item still unsplit on side-live, not on the dropped list, no repair note, no new nodes. Statement correction: the delivery adds local centrality of s_A(r)|_U and s_B(r)|_V. It is necessary, because the ringed-topos and module definitions allow noncommutative rings. I rechecked the counterexample on a point topos with A=B=M_2(Q) and t↦diag(1,0): t·id is not A-linear (d·E12=E12 but E12·d=0). The only citer, lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor, uses commutative coefficient sheaves, so it still holds. Steps: (1) the sectionwise R-linear category uses centrality; (2) the transpose formula of def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, with letters reversed, plus c(u^{-1}s_A)=s_B gives F(rf)=rF(f). (3) Mod(B) is Grothendieck by the noncommutative ring-sheaf node; K-injective resolutions exist; Q_A F_K is exact by the cone/biproduct argument; 070K (derived.tex l.9767, read) gives RF. (4) The map-computation node's RF is def-sfb-right-derived-functor, which is defined through the same lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived, so it is the same canonical Ru_*. (5) Uniqueness of the homotopy class, linearity of Q and cancelling the fixed c_a, c_b give additivity and R-linearity of Ru_*. (6) Scalar endomorphisms go to scalar endomorphisms. Edge cases r=0, r=1, R=0 and unbounded complexes are fine. Duplicates: lem-sbc-ambient-operations-scalar-linearity is only the pro-étale, commutative-ring version, and lem-cbc-exact-linear-derived-functor needs F exact; neither restates the item. I accept the three declared tool uses: the noncommutative Grothendieck node, the 070K total-derived node and the ringed-topos definition. No SGA source is used.
